subject: Blue Harbor: control handback & KMS proofs for security review
messages:
From: Ellen Park <ellen.park@blueharbortrust.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: security@blueharbortrust.com
Date: Fri, 01 Dec 2028 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Request: KMS rotation proofs + control mapping for procurement security review

Hi Vanessa,

We’re in the final leg of Blue Harbor’s procurement security review and need a concise packet that ties your controls to our questionnaire (SIG + ISO 27001) and includes KMS/key rotation proof artifacts. Specifically, the security team asked for: 

- A control crosswalk that maps SIG v2 and ISO 27001 clauses to Redwood controls (owner and evidence file name).
- Recent KMS rotation logs for the last 6 months (audit entries, rotation timestamps, and who triggered rotation).
- A short diagram showing how keys are provisioned and where they live (Cloud KMS / HSM / customer-managed).
- A summary of your key retention and destruction policy (one paragraph).

Can you provide those items as a secure bundle within 48 hours? If you prefer, we can stand up an SFTP or accept a pre-signed S3 upload; please advise the preferred method. Also, which SIG version should we reference in the mapping?

We’ll treat the artifacts as confidential — happy to sign an NDA if needed, but the procurement folks would like delivery & intake instructions.

Thanks,
Ellen Park
Head of Security Operations
Blue Harbor Trust
ellen.park@blueharbortrust.com

Attachment: BlueHarbor_SecurityQuestionnaire_v3.xlsx (referenced)
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ellen Park <ellen.park@blueharbortrust.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwoodinference.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 01 Dec 2028 10:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Request: KMS rotation proofs + control mapping for procurement security review

Hi Ellen — thanks for the clear list. We can get an initial packet over within your 48-hour window.

Quick answers up-front:
- Use SIG v2 for the mapping (we’ll label each sheet with the version).
- Preferred intake: pre-signed, scoped S3 upload (link will be valid 72 hours) — we’ll also provide a Google Drive link if you require G Suite audit controls.

Planned deliverables:
1) redwood_control-mapping-SIG-v2.xlsx — crosswalk (control, redwood control id, evidence file names, owner)
2) redwood_iso27001-clauses-crosswalk.docx — short crosswalk calling out relevant clauses
3) redwood_kms-architecture-diagram.pdf — high-level key lifecycle and boundary diagram
4) redwood_kms-rotation-export-20281201.csv — export of rotation/audit entries (redacted user identifiers where required)
5) one-page retention/destruction summary in the packet

Internal owners: I’m looping in Kimberly (Compliance) to author the crosswalk and the 1‑page policy, and Jonas (Assurance Ops) to pull the KMS rotation export and validate the audit entries.

If you need the items in a specific file naming convention for ingestion, send a sample and we’ll mirror it. We’ll follow up with the secure upload link within 6 hours and expect to complete the packet early tomorrow.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Director, Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference
vanessa@redwoodinference.com
Phone: +1 (415) 555-0134
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwoodinference.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwoodinference.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 01 Dec 2028 13:22:00 -08:00
Subject: Blue Harbor packet — assignments and timeline

Kimberly / Jonas — forwarding Ellen’s ask (below). Target: initial packet by 10:00 AM PT tomorrow so procurement can start intake.

Kimberly — please produce the crosswalk (SIG v2 tab + ISO crosswalk docx) and the 1‑page retention/destruction summary. Use the naming convention I listed and mark any evidence that contains PII as REDACTED and call that out in the mapping.

Jonas — pull the KMS rotation audit export for the last 6 months and normalize to CSV. Redact full user identifiers per policy but include timestamps, rotation type (automatic/manual), and trigger source (API/console). Also attach the KMS architecture diagram (I attached an existing draft).

Notes:
- If logs include customer-specific key aliases, replace actual aliases with alias-<redacted-n>.
- We’ll provide a pre-signed S3 link; set object ACL to private and list access principals in the HubSpot ticket.
- If either of you foresee blockers (legal redaction, long export times), flag immediately.

Thanks — I’ll create the upload link and send to Ellen once we have the files.

To: Ellen Park <ellen.park@blueharbortrust.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwoodinference.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, 02 Dec 2028 15:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Blue Harbor: secure packet upload + artifacts (SIG v2 / ISO crosswalks + KMS logs)

Hi Ellen — thanks for the patience. We’ve assembled the initial packet and uploaded it via a secure, time‑bound channel. Summary and access below.

What’s included (file list):
- redwood_control-mapping-SIG-v2.xlsx (SIG v2 mapping, control owners, evidence file pointers)
- redwood_iso27001-clauses-crosswalk.docx (ISO 27001 clause map and brief notes)
- redwood_kms-architecture-diagram.pdf (key lifecycle: generation, storage, rotation, revocation)
- redwood_kms-rotation-export-20281201.csv (normalized export: timestamp, rotation_type, trigger_source, key_alias_redacted)
- redwood_retention-destruction-summary.pdf (one‑page policy)

Intake / access:
- Secure upload (pre-signed S3): https://s3.redwoodinference.com/upload/BH-BUNDLE-20281201 (link expires 72 hours)
- Google Drive alternative (view-only, restricted): https://drive.google.com/secure/drive/folders/1a2B3cSharedPacket?usp=sharing

Reference ticket: HubSpot HS-48291 — I’ve listed internal access principals (Vanessa/Kimberly/Jonas) and the Blue Harbor reviewer group.

Short clarifications: 
- SIG version: v2 (sheet labeled accordingly).
- User identifiers in the rotation export are redacted to alias-<redacted-n> per our data handling policy. If you need unmapped identifiers under an executed NDA, we can discuss next steps and legal review.
- Retention/destruction: keys are rotated automatically every 90 days for service keys; customer-managed keys follow customer policy. The one‑page summary contains retention windows and destruction mechanics (KMS-wipe + HSM zeroization).

If you prefer a short handover call to walk through the packet, I’m available Monday 10–12 PT.

Regards,
Vanessa Ortiz
Director, Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference
vanessa@redwoodinference.com
Phone: +1 (415) 555-0134

Attachments (delivered via link): redwood_kms-rotation-export-20281201.csv, redwood_kms-architecture-diagram.pdf, redwood_control-mapping-SIG-v2.xlsx, redwood_iso27001-clauses-crosswalk.docx
